2. Regulatory framework and scope

The use of cookies and technologies that store or access information on a user’s device is governed, among other applicable rules, by Article 22.2 of Spanish Law 34/2002 on information society services and electronic commerce (LSSI). Where these technologies involve the processing of personal data, Regulation (EU) 2016/679 (GDPR) and the relevant Spanish data protection legislation also apply.

Cookies that are strictly necessary to transmit a communication or provide a service expressly requested by the user may be exempt from the consent requirement. Non-essential cookies will only be activated where there is a valid legal basis and, where appropriate, after the user has given valid consent.
3. What are cookies and similar technologies?

Cookies are small text files that a website can store in a user’s browser or device. Technologies with similar functions may also be used, such as local storage, pixels, technical identifiers or embedded scripts.

These technologies may enable the technical operation of the site, remember preferences, maintain security, manage sessions, measure page usage or, where appropriate and with consent, personalise content or commercial communications.
4. Types of cookies by purpose
Technical or strictly necessary cookies

These enable basic site operation, browsing, security, load balancing, fraud or bot prevention, session management, retention of cookie choices or the provision of a function expressly requested by the user. Where strictly necessary, they will not be used for incompatible additional purposes.
Preference or functional cookies

These remember user choices, such as language or certain interface preferences. Where the rules require consent for a specific preference, the corresponding technology will remain disabled until consent is obtained.
Analytics or performance cookies

These measure, in aggregate, how a site is used, detect errors, identify visited pages or improve performance. Where consent is required, they will not be installed or activated before the user accepts them.
Advertising or marketing cookies
These may measure campaigns, limit repeated advertisements, create audiences or display interest-based advertising. If used, any required prior consent will be requested.
Cookies or technologies of embedded services

Certain pages may include forms, calendars, CRM, chat, video, maps, captchas or other third-party components. Their purpose and consent requirements will depend on the component and the technologies it actually loads in the browser.
5. First-party and third-party cookies
Depending on the entity managing the technology, the sites may use:
First-party cookies: managed from domains or components controlled by Rooklyn.
Third-party cookies: managed by technology providers integrated into the site when the relevant function is active.
The actual presence of a particular cookie may vary according to the domain visited, the page, the loaded component, the technical configuration and the user’s choice in the consent manager.

7. Consent and settings
Where cookies or technologies requiring consent are used, users will have clear mechanisms, from the first layer or banner, to:
Accept non-essential cookies.
Reject non-essential cookies.
Configure cookies by purpose and save their selection.

Accept and reject options must be offered at the same time and with equivalent visibility. Pre-selected boxes will not be used, and merely continuing to browse will not be treated as consent. Non-essential cookies requiring consent will remain blocked until the user makes a valid choice.
8. Withdrawing or changing consent
Users may change or withdraw their preferences at any time through the “Cookie settings” link or button permanently available in the footer or in the site’s consent management system.

Withdrawing consent does not affect the lawfulness of processing carried out before withdrawal. When a user rejects a category, technologies in that category will no longer load on subsequent visits, except those that are strictly necessary or must be retained to comply with a legal obligation.
9. Browser settings

In addition to the site’s consent manager, users can allow, block, delete or limit cookies through their browser settings. Blocking certain technical cookies may prevent some requested functions from being provided correctly.
Major browsers include specific privacy and cookie options in their settings menus (for example, Chrome, Edge, Firefox and Safari). The procedure may vary by version and device.

Where any such service installs non-essential cookies or uses non-essential tracking technologies, the corresponding consent requirements will apply.

11. International transfers

Some technology providers may process data outside the European Economic Area. Where personal data are transferred internationally, Rooklyn will seek to ensure that a mechanism recognised by applicable rules is used, such as an adequacy decision, the EU–US Data Privacy Framework (where the provider is certified and the transfer is covered) or standard contractual clauses, as appropriate.

HighLevel publicly states that HighLevel and LeadConnector participate in the EU–US Data Privacy Framework. To learn about the specific mechanism applicable to a given processing activity, consult the provider’s privacy documentation and Rooklyn’s Privacy Policy.
12. Retention

Session cookies are normally deleted when the browser is closed. Persistent cookies remain for the configured period or until the user deletes them. Rooklyn will apply retention periods proportionate to the purpose and periodically review active technologies to avoid unnecessary retention.
13. Updates to this Policy

This Policy may be updated when the cookies used, technology providers, domains managed by Rooklyn or applicable legal obligations change. The date of the latest update will appear at the beginning of the document. We recommend reviewing this page periodically.
